bugs: original_name is stored as-is from the client with no length cap. A client filename over 255 characters would fail the insert on a strict MySQL string(255) column (app/Http/Controllers/DocumentController.php:23). This is an edge case.
antipatterns: Files are stored on the implicit default disk (`$file->store('documents')`, `Storage::exists`, `Storage::download`), so whether confidential files stay private depends on the FILESYSTEM_DISK env value (app/Http/Controllers/DocumentController.php:22,32,41-43)
Uses the string rule 'mimes:pdf,png,jpg,jpeg' and 'max:5120' instead of the fluent File::types()->max() rule (app/Http/Requests/StoreDocumentRequest.php:12)
Calls Gate::authorize inside the controller instead of declaring ->can('view','document') on the route (app/Http/Controllers/DocumentController.php:31). This is minor.

The 'downloads without login' test still has Sanctum::actingAs active when it hits the signed URL, so it doesn't prove the link works for a guest. It also never checks the file contents (tests/Feature/DocumentTest.php:101-112)
Packs several validation scenarios into one test method (tests/Feature/DocumentTest.php:67-89)
strengths: Compact, correct design: one resource controller, a policy that returns denyAsNotFound(), and a temporarySignedRoute that expires after 10 minutes
Checks ownership before checking whether the file exists, so the 404 for a missing file can't be used to probe other users' documents
The download route is outside auth and uses 'signed' middleware. Storage::download sends Content-Disposition: attachment, and the fallback name handles Unicode and '%' correctly (probe)
Uses the #[Fillable] attribute and creates the row through the relation ($request->user()->documents()->create)

Probes passed: text and SVG files disguised as PDF/PNG are rejected (422), a tampered expires value is rejected (403), and the stored path is a random hash name with an extension guessed from the content
Good test coverage: expiry boundary at 9 and 11 minutes, file vanishing after a link was issued, unknown ID, guest, other user

antipatterns: DocumentFactory has no user_id default, so Document::factory()->create() without ->for() hits a NOT NULL failure (database/factories/DocumentFactory.php:13-19)
Http::preventStrayRequests() in setUp does nothing here because the feature makes no HTTP calls (tests/Feature/DocumentTest.php:22)
Splits the feature into three controllers (store, link and download), which adds a little ceremony for three small actions
Document::DISK as a public const on the model works, but a named private disk in config would be more conventional (app/Models/Document.php:17)
strengths: Pins the private 'local' disk explicitly through Document::DISK, so where confidential files are stored doesn't depend on FILESYSTEM_DISK
Validates with the modern fluent rule File::types(['pdf','png','jpg','jpeg'])->max(5 * 1024)
Authorizes declaratively with ->can('view','document') on the route, and the policy returns denyAsNotFound(). The ownership 404 happens before the file-existence check
Caps the stored original_name to the 255-character column with Str::limit
The no-login download test calls forgetGuards(), so it really runs as a guest. It also checks the streamed content and the attachment filename
Has a tampered-link test that swaps the document ID inside a signed URL
Probes passed: disguised text and SVG files rejected, tampered expires rejected with 403, Unicode and '%' filenames handled, response is no-cache, private
Tests are focused, one behaviour each, and include the 5 MB and 100-character boundaries

v.rationale:
I ranked impl-2 first and impl-1 second. Both test suites pass: 15 tests for impl-1, 18 for impl-2.

**Shared behaviour:** Both use the same core design: a form request, a policy that returns denyAsNotFound(), a 10-minute temporarySignedRoute to a signed download route outside auth, and Storage::download for the attachment. They checked the same in every probe:
- Text disguised as a PDF gets 422.
- An SVG disguised as a PNG gets 422.
- A real PDF named .html is stored under a random .pdf name.
- A tampered expires value gets 403.
- Unicode and '%' in the filename produce a correct Content-Disposition.

Neither has a real functional bug.

**Why impl-2 ranks higher:** The difference is in idioms and how robust the confidential storage is:
- It pins the private disk explicitly. impl-1 relies on the default disk, which an env value can change.
- It uses the fluent File::types()->max() rule.
- It declares authorization on the route with ->can().
- It caps original_name at the column length.
- Its download test calls forgetGuards(), so it really proves the link works without logging in, and it checks the file contents. impl-1's equivalent test still has a logged-in Sanctum user.

**Where impl-2 loses points:**
- Three controllers instead of one.
- A factory without a user_id default.
- An unneeded Http::preventStrayRequests() in the tests.

**impl-1:** It's slightly simpler. It's a solid second.
